unit.title: Who does what to what
unit.blurb: Subject, object and verb in whole sentences
unit.intro: A Latin sentence tells you who does what with word endings, not word order. The subject is nominative (_puer_), the thing acted on is accusative (_pānem_), and the verb ending agrees with the subject: _puer pānem edit_ (the boy eats bread), _puerī pānem edunt_ (the boys eat bread). Because the endings carry the meaning, the same sentence can be written in any order. With _ego_, _tū_ and _nōs_ left out, the verb ending alone says who it is: _pānem edō_, _pānem edis_.

templates.explain: _{s}_ is {s.label}, the subject; _{v}_ ({v.lemma}) is {v.label}, agreeing with it. _{o}_ is {o.label}: the thing the verb acts on.

roles.s: it is the subject of the sentence, so it must be nominative
roles.o: it is the object (the thing acted on), so it must be accusative
